items.title: Multiple Roads Shut Near Creditview and Sherwood Mills After Driver Strikes Pedestrian
items.summary: Peel Regional Police shut down several roads near Creditview Road on Tuesday morning after a vehicle struck a pedestrian in Mississauga, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that a female pedestrian suffered serious injuries in the collision and was taken by paramedics to a local trauma centre. Police did not release further details about the woman's condition or identity, insauga.com said. The driver involved stayed at the scene following the crash, according to the report. To manage the aftermath, police closed southbound Creditview Road at Willowvale Garden, eastbound Princelea Place toward Creditview Road, and westbound Sherwood Mills Boulevard at Brockworth Drive. Insauga.com noted that officers asked drivers in the area to expect delays and seek alternate routes while the roads remained shut.

items.title: October Sales Data Puts Mississauga's Average Home Price Just Above $927,000
items.summary: Mississauga's average home price slipped 0.2 per cent to $927,521 in October 2026, according to the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board. The board's latest figures showed 508 total home sales in the city last month, with properties sitting on the market for an average of 35 days and 2,342 active listings remaining at month's end. Detached houses accounted for 200 of those sales, averaging 32 days on the market, with 894 such listings still active when October closed. Semi-detached homes saw 67 sales and an average of 29 days on the market, leaving 204 active listings. Attached houses were the slowest-moving segment, with just 17 sales and an average of 30 days on the market against 63 active listings. Townhouse-style condos recorded 94 sales over an average of 35 days on the market, with 356 listings still active at month's end, the board's figures showed.

items.title: Peel Police Close Burnhamthorpe Road After Driver Strikes Pedestrian Near Square One
items.summary: Peel Regional Police closed a stretch of Burnhamthorpe Road on Monday after a driver struck a pedestrian near the Square One shopping centre, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that a woman in her 30s was hit by a vehicle near the intersection of Burnhamthorpe Road and Duke of York Boulevard, and that the same vehicle then struck a nearby pole. Police say the woman was rushed to a local trauma centre, though they have not commented on the severity of her injuries, insauga.com said. The outlet noted the driver remained at the scene following the collision. Police closed Burnhamthorpe Road between Duke of York Boulevard and Living Arts Drive as a result, and insauga.com reported that drivers were being told to expect delays and avoid the area if possible.

items.title: City Says Harassment of Mississauga Parking Officers Shows No Sign of Easing
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says harassment of its parking enforcement officers is continuing to be a problem as they carry out their duties across the city, according to insauga.com. City spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told the outlet on Monday that the issue persists, saying in an email that parking enforcement officers continue to face harassment as part of their daily duties. The city has previously said officers have been verbally abused, threatened, spat on and, at times, physically attacked while issuing tickets, insauga.com reported. The outlet noted the city declined to comment on specific incidents, citing employee privacy and the integrity of police investigations or legal proceedings that could arise from the confrontations. Some incidents have led to arrests and charges, and the city says it takes seriously any case in which officers are inappropriately confronted by upset drivers.

items.title: City Centre Transit Terminal Platforms to Close in Stages Through Nov. 20 for LRT Construction
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says platforms at the City Centre Transit Terminal near Square One Shopping Centre will close in stages between Nov. 10 and Nov. 20 as construction continues on the $6-billion Hazel McCallion Line, according to insauga.com. City officials said the closures, which affect areas both inside and outside the terminal, are needed as light-rail transit work connecting Mississauga and Brampton ramps up in the downtown core. The terminal itself will stay open during regular operating hours throughout the work, the city added. Officials urged MiWay riders to plan ahead and watch for posted notices to find their new bus stop locations during the affected period. The city said bus routes will keep running on their regular schedules, with only the platform locations changing. Full overnight closures are planned for Nov. 14 and several other nights, insauga.com reported, when no buses will serve their usual platforms inside the terminal.

items.title: Thousands of Local Votes Decide Mississauga's 2026 Readers' Choice Award Winners
items.summary: Thousands of Mississauga residents nominated and voted for their favourite local businesses in the 2026 Readers' Choice Awards, according to Mississauga.com. The outlet reported the finalists span nine categories, including Automotive, Food & Drink, Home Improvement, and Kids & Pets, highlighting businesses that readers say stand out for consistently good service. Mississauga.com said the top three vote-getters in each category earned diamond, platinum or gold recognition based on how they do business, rather than through any paid promotion. The outlet noted the rankings reflect real customer experiences, since the winners were chosen entirely by people who walked through their doors and came away with a memorable visit. Mississauga.com is encouraging residents to look through the full list of finalists and recognize their favourites on social media.

items.title: Rotary Club of Mississauga Taps Casino Charitable Gaming Program After 72 Years of Service
items.summary: The Rotary Club of Mississauga has received a licence to take part in charitable gaming at Rama Gaming House in Meadowvale, giving the 72-year-old service club a new source of fundraising, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported the arrangement connects one of Mississauga's oldest service organizations with an established program that has become an important revenue source for non-profits across the city. Rather than receiving a straightforward donation, insauga.com said participating organizations contribute volunteer hours at the gaming centre and receive a share of proceeds based on hours worked. Other groups already associated with Rama's charitable gaming program include Hospice Mississauga, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Peel, the Boys & Girls Club of Peel, Gymnastics Mississauga, the Art Gallery of Mississauga and the Mississauga Arts Council, the outlet noted. The program is run through Ontario's charitable gaming system, which involves the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation, private gaming operators, municipalities and approved charities, and insauga.com reported it has generated hundreds of millions of dollars for community groups across the province since it began.

items.title: Streetsville Hairstylist Doubles as Gallery Owner at Heartbreak Hotel
items.summary: Omar Preza has turned his Streetsville barbershop, Heartbreak Hotel, into more than a place for haircuts, according to the Toronto Star. The newspaper reported that Preza, 44, was born in El Salvador and raised in Canada, and built the shop around his lifelong passions for drawing, collecting superhero comics and admiring street graffiti. Inside, the Star said, upbeat Latin and hip-hop music plays while painted canvases in thrifted gold frames and custom apparel hang from industrial pipe racks against black-and-white brick walls. According to the newspaper, Heartbreak Hotel began in 2013 as a streetwear clothing brand, with Preza starting to paint around the same time, and he now sells both original fine art and custom-designed apparel alongside the haircuts. The Star noted his work was included in the Art Gallery of Mississauga's 2024-2025 Fourth Annual Juried Show of Visual Arts.

items.title: Mississauga-Raised Netflix Star Helps Nintendo Launch Ocarina of Time Remake in Toronto
items.summary: Mississauga native Maitreyi Ramakrishnan joined Nintendo of Canada in Toronto on Nov. 5 to help launch the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that Ramakrishnan, best known for her breakout role in the Netflix series Never Have I Ever, grew up in Mississauga and attended Meadowvale Secondary School. She told insauga.com she has been a die-hard fan of Nintendo and the Zelda franchise since she was five years old, and called the graphics on the Nintendo Switch especially striking. The outlet noted Ocarina of Time remains one of the franchise's most iconic and culturally influential titles more than 25 years after its original debut. Ramakrishnan graduated from York University in 2025 while continuing to work on film and television projects, insauga.com said. Her most recent role came in Best of the Best, a film about two lifelong friends who join a university Bollywood-fusion dance squad, which premiered on Netflix in September.
